By waiting for Ruin Crab #2 to resolve and casting Hedron Crab first, the Delta crack would trigger all 3 crabs (2 Ruin Crabs + Hedron Crab) for 9 mill instead of 3, losing 6 cards of mill. Additionally, playing Cephalid Coliseum after all crabs are in play would maximize further triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Polluted Delta before letting the second Ruin Crab resolve and before casting Hedron Crab, getting only 3 cards of mill from the fetch.
annotations.betterLine: Let Ruin Crab #2 resolve, cast Hedron Crab using Island, then crack Polluted Delta to trigger all 3 crabs for 9 mill, then play Cephalid Coliseum for another 9 mill (18 total vs ~6 from suboptimal sequencing).

annotations.description: Fetched a basic Island when the player has Glimpse the Unthinkable (UB) in hand and no black mana sources on the battlefield. Fetching Watery Grave (paying 2 life to enter untapped) would have enabled casting Glimpse the Unthinkable this turn alongside playing Cephalid Coliseum or another land, providing a huge mill tempo advantage. A basic Swamp would also have been better to enable Glimpse next turn without life loss.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched basic Island from Polluted Delta
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Watery Grave (pay 2 life, enter untapped) to have access to black mana, enabling Glimpse the Unthinkable to be cast this turn or next turn. This maximizes the mill gameplan's speed.

annotations.description: Playing Urza's Saga as the land drop triggers all three of opponent's crabs (2 Ruin Crab + 1 Hedron Crab) to mill 9 cards total, directly fueling the opponent's mill gameplan. Against a dedicated mill deck, unnecessary land drops that trigger landfall are very costly.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Urza's Saga from hand, triggering 9 cards milled from the three crabs.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Emry, Lurker of the Loch using Mox Opal for {U} (affinity reduces cost from {2}{U} to {U} with 3 artifacts), developing a threat that enables recurring Arcbound Ravager and Lavaspur Boots from graveyard, without triggering opponent's landfall mill. Hold the Urza's Saga for a turn where playing a land is more necessary or when crabs have been dealt with.

annotations.description: Casting a second Mox Opal from hand when one is already on the battlefield is problematic due to the legend rule. The player will have to sacrifice one of the two Mox Opals immediately. While this does trigger Weapons Manufacturing (creating another Munitions token) and the legend rule sacrifice could feed Arcbound Ravager if it were on the battlefield, the Ravager is in the graveyard. The player is essentially spending a card from hand just to get a Munitions token and a Weapons Manufacturing trigger. However, casting Emry first would have been better sequencing - Emry has affinity for artifacts and already costs very little with the artifacts in play, and Emry could then tap to recur an artifact from the graveyard (like Arcbound Ravager or Lavaspur Boots). The Mox Opal play does create value through Weapons Manufacturing, but losing a card permanently for just a Munitions token when Emry could provide recurring value seems suboptimal.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Mox Opal from hand, triggering the legend rule and losing one copy, but generating a Munitions token from Weapons Manufacturing.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Emry, Lurker of the Loch first (costs only U with affinity from 4+ artifacts), mill four cards to fuel graveyard, then use Emry to recur key artifacts. The Mox Opal could still be played afterward if needed for the Weapons Manufacturing trigger.

annotations.description: Against a dedicated mill deck with Ruin Crabs and Hedron Crab, casting Emry mills 4 additional cards from your own library, actively advancing the opponent's win condition. With already 10 cards in graveyard, this accelerates the clock significantly.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Emry, Lurker of the Loch, self-milling 4 cards against a mill opponent.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Urza's Saga to create a Construct token (likely 5/5+), which also triggers Weapons Manufacturing for a Munitions token, building board pressure without self-milling. Emry's recursive value is strong but the self-mill cost is particularly painful in this matchup.

annotations.description: Field of Ruin is significantly better here than Watery Grave. The opponent has two Urza's Sagas on the battlefield, which are extremely dangerous enchantment lands that will create large Construct tokens and tutor for artifacts. Field of Ruin can destroy one of them. More importantly, when Field of Ruin is activated, both players search their libraries, which enables Archive Trap to be cast for free (0 mana) to mill 13 cards. The player has Archive Trap in hand, so playing Field of Ruin sets up a devastating sequence: activate Field of Ruin to destroy an Urza's Saga, trigger the library search, then cast Archive Trap for free, all while triggering the three crabs from both the Field of Ruin land drop AND the basic land entering from Field of Ruin's effect (two landfall triggers). Watery Grave tapped provides mana fixing but no immediate impact and misses the Field of Ruin + Archive Trap synergy.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Watery Grave (tapped) as the land drop for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Field of Ruin to trigger all three crabs (mill 9), then on a future turn activate Field of Ruin to destroy an Urza's Saga, triggering opponent's library search to enable free Archive Trap (mill 13), plus getting another land enter trigger for the crabs (mill 9 more). Alternatively, if the player wanted both blue and black mana available, they could still prioritize Field of Ruin since Glimpse the Unthinkable requires UB and can wait, but removing Urza's Saga and enabling Archive Trap is far more impactful.

annotations.description: With Emry untapped and a graveyard full of powerful artifacts (Shadowspear, Arcbound Ravager, Mishra's Bauble, Lavaspur Boots), the player should be activating Emry to target an artifact to cast this turn. Against mill crabs that are rapidly depleting the library, tempo is critical and every resource should be utilized. Tapping Emry for Shadowspear or Arcbound Ravager would significantly advance the board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Appeared to pass without activating Emry, Lurker of the Loch, waiting for Saga triggers to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Tap Emry targeting a high-value artifact in the graveyard (Shadowspear for lifelink/trample, Arcbound Ravager for sacrifice synergy, or Mishra's Bauble for a free artifact + card draw) to maximize resources before the mill crabs deplete the library further.

annotations.description: Archive Trap is on the stack about to mill 13 cards. With 24 cards already in the graveyard, the player is in serious danger of being decked. The opponent's entire strategy is mill, and letting a free 13-card mill resolve when you have a counter available is potentially game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority on Archive Trap instead of countering it, apparently confused about the stack contents (thought it was a Bauble).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Metallic Rebuke targeting Archive Trap, using Mox Opal for {U} and tapping 2 artifacts for improvise to pay the {2}{U} cost. Countering a 13-card mill spell is critical to survival in this matchup.

annotations.description: Cephalid Coliseum taps for U but deals 1 damage to self, and its threshold ability requires 7+ cards in graveyard (Coach only has 3). Field of Ruin produces colorless but can destroy opponent's Urza's Saga and when activated later, both players searching for basics triggers additional landfall mill from the crabs. Both lands enable Glimpse the Unthinkable this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Cephalid Coliseum as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Field of Ruin to have future utility destroying opponent's nonbasic lands and generating additional landfall triggers when activated, while still being able to cast Glimpse the Unthinkable this turn

annotations.description: Failed to activate Mishra's Bauble for free card advantage. With the player's library being heavily milled by opponent's crabs, every card draw matters. Mishra's Bauble activation is essentially free - it draws a card next upkeep and provides information. Emry can also recast it from the graveyard later if needed. Metalcraft would still be active (4 artifacts remaining).

annotations.betterLine: Activate Mishra's Bauble targeting opponent's library (for information) to get a free card draw at next upkeep, then pass priority
